milestone.title: mp watch end-to-end against herdr 0.7.x — harness defaults, spawn API realignment, spawn diagnostics, watch readiness parity

intent.outcome: mp watch successfully drives a milestone execute → complete against the current stable herdr (0.7.x) end-to-end. Harness config has sensible defaults; herdr spawn API is realigned to current stable herdr; spawn failures are loud in log, status, and exit code; mp doctor and execution check reflect real watch readiness (harness config + herdr CLI compatibility).

problem.description: From mp-watch-issues.md (andre dogfood, 2026-07-23) — five issues make mp watch unusable end-to-end against herdr 0.7.5: (A) no default agent runner/coordinator harness config (mp watch refuses on a fresh project); (B, hard blocker) herdr argv mismatch — mp emits `herdr agent start role-runner-1 --cwd <path> -- opencode` but herdr 0.7.5 wants `agent start <NAME> --kind <KIND> --pane <ID> [OPTIONS]` (mp treats herdr as create-labeled-agent + cwd, herdr wants start-known-kind-in-existing-pane); (C) silent spawn failure — log shows boot → state_persisted → read_milestone → ensure_pane only, no stderr, no exit code, run_state goes stale; (E) mp execution check / handoff reports ready while watch preconditions are red. The existing M149 (watch automation, complete) was built against a different herdr API and has drifted. No open milestone covers the herdr-0.7.x realignment or the diagnostics gap. (Issue D — verify-ac `unknown` noise — is already addressed by completed M177, verification gate hardening.) The desired outcome for the next mp release per the report: spawn succeeds against current stable herdr; spawn failures are loud; doctor/execution check reflect real watch readiness.

in_scope: Default agent harness config: during `mp init` (primary, user-driven path) when exactly one harness skill is installed and `agent.runner.harness` / `agent.coordinator.harness` are unset, auto-set both to the available harness. Lazy fallback on first `mp watch` invocation if not already set. Surface the auto-set value in `mp doctor` (UI section). On multiple installed harnesses, surface the ambiguity in `mp doctor` instead of picking.

herdr spawn API realignment: update mp watch herdr integration to herdr 0.7.x shape — create/ensure the runner pane via herdr pane APIs (workspace/tab/pane), then `herdr agent start <name> --kind opencode --pane <id>`. cwd is a pane property (set during pane create) or a follow-up pane set-cwd command, whichever herdr 0.7.x exposes. Verify against the current stable herdr release.

Version gate: `mp doctor` and `mp watch` preconditions detect herdr CLI shape (e.g. `herdr agent start --help` contains the expected flags); fail fast with a clear `mp X requires herdr >= Y` message instead of a silent crash after boot.

Spawn diagnostics: on any herdr command failure, append a structured `spawn_error` event to watch.log capturing full argv, stdout, stderr, and exit status; set run_state to a terminal failure kind (distinct from `stale`); exit non-zero from the foreground watch driver when spawn fails.

Watch readiness parity: fold watch preconditions (harness config + herdr CLI compat) into `mp execution check` / `execution handoff` so a single readiness signal reflects real watch spawnability (per DD-04). The two signals in `mp doctor` (readiness check, M198 `ui.show_watch_tab` value) are explicitly independent and named distinctly.
out_of_scope: M149 is not reopened for re-derivation; this milestone builds on M149 and adds the herdr-0.7.x realignment + diagnostics + readiness parity.

Issue D (verify-ac `unknown` noise) — already addressed by completed M177. If M177's heuristic misses specific prose forms during execution, file a follow-up milestone (Q-01 resolution); not folded into M197's scope.
Fixing andre M01 S3 — separate; per the report's non-goals, will run manually or after the watch fix lands.
Changing herdr itself or shipping a legacy herdr pin — file separately against the herdr project if needed; mp adapts to current stable herdr.

acceptance_criteria.description: Default harness config: during `mp init` (primary path, user-driven), when exactly one harness skill is installed and `agent.runner.harness` / `agent.coordinator.harness` are unset, auto-set both. Lazy fallback on first `mp watch` invocation if not already set. The auto-set value is surfaced in `mp doctor` (UI section). On multiple installed harnesses, surface the ambiguity in `mp doctor` instead of picking.
acceptance_criteria.verification: manual: accepted — fresh-project fixture (mp init, one harness installed) reaches mp watch preconditions green; multi-harness fixture surfaces the ambiguity in doctor; lazy-fallback fixture (init not run, mp watch run first) auto-sets on first watch invocation.
acceptance_criteria.evidence:
M197 end-to-end: mp watch against herdr 0.7.x spawn shape with harness defaults, spawn API realignment, spawn diagnostics, and watch readiness parity across execution surfaces.

Work packages (all done):
- WP1 (S1 / AC-01): harness auto-set on `mp init` + lazy fallback on first `mp watch` + `mp doctor` surface. New `crates/mp/src/harness/auto.rs` with `detect_installed_harnesses` + `auto_set_target` (unit-tested). Wired into `store::init_plan_inner` (init), `watch::try_lazy_auto_set` (lazy fallback, persisted via `store::write_config`), and `doctor::doctor_project` (harness_auto_set check that surfaces AutoSet / NoOp / Ambiguous).
- WP2 (S2 / AC-03): herdr 0.7.x two-step spawn shape — `herdr pane split --cwd <PATH>` followed by `herdr agent start <NAME> --kind <KIND> --pane <PANE_ID>`. Refactored `crates/mp/src/watch/herdr.rs` to drop the legacy `--cwd` / `--` separator shape. New `resolve_harness_kind` replaces `resolve_harness_argv` (the harness kind is a closed enum on herdr's side). Dry-run preview in `mp watch` emits both steps as separate `herdr_commands` entries.
- WP3 (S3 / AC-02 + S4 / AC-04): herdr CLI version + shape gate (new `crates/mp/src/watch/herdr_version.rs` with `detect_herdr_cli` / `HerdCliShape`), plus structured spawn diagnostics (new `SpawnFailure` type, `extract_spawn_failure` helper, `WatchLogEntry::spawn_error` builder, `RunOutcome::SpawnFailed` + `DriveOutcome::SpawnFailed` variants, sequencer halt-on-SpawnFailed). All wired into `mp doctor`, watch preconditions, the state machine, and the v2 control-plane state.
- WP4 (S5 / AC-05): watch readiness folded into `execution::check` / `execution_handoff` / `execution_status`. `ExecutionCheckReport` now carries a `WatchReadiness` struct that mirrors the `mp watch` precondition report. `can_handoff` is gated on watch readiness when the plan is in autonomous mode, with a `warnings` line that names the failed preconditions. One canonical precondition function powers `mp execution check`, `mp watch start`, and `mp milestone handoff`.

Verification (live run):
- `cargo nextest run -p mp --lib --no-fail-fast` → 376/376 passed (full mp lib suite, includes execution::execution_check_with).
- `cargo nextest run -p mp --test watch_herdr_start --no-fail-fast` → 15/15 passed (the spawn-shape contract is pinned against a fake herdr).
- `cargo nextest run -p mp --test watch_spawn_diagnostics --no-fail-fast` → 9/9 passed (SpawnFailure round-trip + WatchLogEntry spawn_error shape).
- `cargo nextest run -p mp --test watch_log_prompt_source --no-fail-fast` → 10/10 passed.
- `cargo nextest run -p mp --test watch_execution --no-fail-fast` → 8/8 passed.
- `cargo nextest run -p mp --test watch_sequential --no-fail-fast` → 10/10 passed.
- `cargo nextest run -p mp --no-fail-fast -E 'test(/doctor|execution_check|execution_status|execution_handoff|herdr_version|auto_set_target|sequencer|spawn_error|logging::)/'  → 50/50 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p mp --tests --no-deps -- -D warnings` → clean.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` → clean.

Self-review (stage 6): F-01 filed — `crates/mp/tests/watch_non_dry_run.rs::non_dry_run_watch_spawns_herdr_pane_and_sends_prompt` initially failed because the test fixture's log-record parser was brittle under the new fake-herdr's multi-part records. The fixture was fixed during the remediation pass; the test now passes (9/9 in `cargo nextest run -p mp --test watch_non_dry_run`). F-01 closed as `status: fixed, fixed_in: HEAD, resolved: 2026-08-28`.

External review (stage 7, external-reviewer (mavis)): 4 additional low-severity findings filed and fixed in this remediation pass — F-02 (stale plan evidence, fixed by this update), F-03 (misleading Send/Sync comment in `extract_spawn_failure`, fixed by rewording the doc-comment), F-04 (lazy auto-set had no activity event, fixed by adding `lazy_auto_set_event` and wiring it into `watch::try_lazy_auto_set` in `commands/watch.rs`), F-05 (`EXPECTED_START_FLAGS` / version floor not co-versioned, fixed by doc-test `expected_flags_and_version_floor_are_paired` in `watch/herdr_version.rs`). Verdict: ok.

design_decisions.choice: Realign mp to current stable herdr (0.7.x pane-create then agent start --kind --pane). Do not ship or pin a legacy herdr version; do not add an mp compat shim that re-emits the old argv.
design_decisions.rationale: Adapting to the current upstream API is the forward-looking choice; pinning a legacy herdr version couples the mp release to a stale binary and the compat shim path perpetuates the drift. Matches the report's primary suggestion.

design_decisions.choice: Auto-set agent.runner.harness and agent.coordinator.harness from the single installed harness skill on first use (or via mp init); surface the auto-set in mp doctor; include the harness config check in execution handoff so handoff cannot look ready while watch cannot start.
design_decisions.rationale: Silent assumption is dangerous; explicit-but-automatic (surface in doctor) reduces friction on fresh projects while keeping the operator informed. Folding the check into handoff closes the execution-check vs watch readiness gap (Issue E).

design_decisions.choice: Introduce a run_state kind for terminal spawn failure (distinct from stale); capture a structured spawn_error event in watch.log with argv + stdout + stderr + exit; foreground watch exits non-zero on spawn failure.
design_decisions.rationale: The current stale state and silent exit hide the real failure (Issue C); a distinct terminal kind + structured event + non-zero exit makes the failure actionable. Matches the report's suggestion.

design_decisions.choice: Fold harness config and herdr CLI compat into mp execution check / execution handoff so a single readiness signal reflects real watch spawnability (preferred). Fallback: explicitly document two surfaces (execution handoff vs watch) if folding is rejected.
design_decisions.rationale: A single readiness signal avoids the can_handoff:true / watch:red confusion (Issue E). Documentation alone is weaker than a single gate; folding is the stronger fix.

design_decisions.choice: The readiness signal (this milestone, M197) and the `ui.show_watch_tab` user preference (M198) are independent signals that will both appear in `mp doctor`. They will be named distinctly: the readiness line is the watch-capability check (harness config + herdr CLI shape, can mp watch spawn right now), and the preference line is the user-toggle (do I have the watch tab visible in the TUI). A user reading doctor should not confuse them. If the names are too similar, prefix the readiness line (e.g. `watch.preconditions`) and keep the preference line as `ui.show_watch_tab`.
design_decisions.rationale: Both milestones are about the "watch" feature but measure different things. M197 reports capability (herdr shape, harness config). M198 reports preference (user opt-in to the TUI tab). Conflating them in a single doctor line would hide a real capability gap behind a user preference, or vice versa. Explicit separation makes the doctor output actionable.

findings.description:
crates/mp/tests/watch_non_dry_run.rs::non_dry_run_watch_spawns_herdr_pane_and_sends_prompt fails after the M197 spawn-shape realignment. The test installs a fake `herdr` shell script and parses the script's log file to assert that `agent start` was called. The fake was updated for the M197 0.7.x two-step shape (`pane split --cwd <PATH>` followed by `agent start <NAME> --kind <KIND> --pane <ID>`) and to answer `agent start --help` / `pane split --help` so the new herdr_cli_shape precondition gate is green.

The remaining failure is in the test fixture's record parser, not in the production code. The parser reads `<tag-len:4><tag><part-len:4><part>...\n` records and walks the inner loop with a single `\n` check at the end of each part. For multi-part records the parser reads the next record's bytes as parts of the current record and then misaligns by 1-4 bytes on the next record, which causes the `find` for `tag=agent, parts[0]=start` to miss the real `agent start` record. The pre-existing fixture was tolerant of this for the legacy spawn shape because the legacy fake produced records with at most one part; the new shape (and the new fake's `--help` and `pane split` answers) exposes the bug.

The fix is to rewrite the parser to track the record terminator `\n` correctly (read exactly the bytes declared by each length prefix, then expect `\n` as the next byte) — a small fixture change, not a production change. Filed as backlog so the next dogfood pass can clean it up alongside the wider M197 wp2 fallout (any other fake-herdr test that assumes the legacy argv shape will need a similar update).
findings.summary: watch_non_dry_run fixture parser brittle under M197 spawn-shape realignment

crates/mp/src/watch/herdr.rs:283-298: the comment on extract_spawn_failure says 'SpawnFailure derives neither Send nor Sync, so callers should not expect to cross thread boundaries with one.' This is incorrect - all fields of SpawnFailure (String, Vec<String>, Option<i32>) are Send+Sync, so the type is auto-Send+Sync by default. The comment is misleading. Either (a) remove the comment if no thread-crossing concern exists, or (b) add an explicit negative impl (impl !Send for SpawnFailure {} via PhantomData) if the intent is to opt out. Current code has neither: the type is Send+Sync, the comment says it isn't, and there's no test pinning either behavior. The mp watch driver is single-threaded today, so this is latent, not active.

crates/mp/src/commands/watch.rs:84-95: try_lazy_auto_set persists a config change when AutoSet fires, but the only audit trail is the persisted config.json itself. There is no activity.json event for the lazy auto-set. Operators checking activity.json (or the dogfood log filter) cannot see the lazy fallback firing - a future 'why did my harness change' investigation will not have a structured trace. Recommend emitting a 'lazy_auto_set' activity event when try_lazy_auto_set transitions to AutoSet so the activity feed captures the auto-set path symmetrically with the explicit mp init path.
findings.summary: Lazy auto-set has no activity event

findings.description: crates/mp/src/watch/herdr_version.rs:45: REQUIRED_HERDR_VERSION_FLOOR is documented as informational - the actual capability test is the EXPECTED_START_FLAGS check on 'agent start --help'. This is correct. But the constant is never updated when EXPECTED_START_FLAGS changes; if herdr 0.8.x renames --kind to --harness, the shape check will fail (good) and the version check will say 'AtOrAbove' (misleading). Recommend a compile-time or doc-test assertion that ties the two together: either a unit test asserting version-floor bumps when EXPECTED_START_FLAGS changes, or an inline comment in EXPECTED_START_FLAGS that flags it as a breaking-change contract.
findings.summary: EXPECTED_START_FLAGS / version floor are not co-versioned
